title: ECOSITY: New Dawn on Mars
summary: A 3D shop-management and gardening simulation set on Mars, built in Unreal Engine by a team of seven over one year.
overview: ECOSITY is a game developed as a course project in the GameTech study program. Created by a team of 7 people, this project was worked on across semesters 3 and 4 over a span of 1 year, featuring a shop management simulation genre with a vegetable garden theme. Designed for Windows, the game has 3D visuals and aims to teach players effective management skills and techniques for growing high-quality vegetables.

In ECOSITY, you are a volunteer sent to Mars to help establish a sustainable colony. To survive, you must grow crops, manage resources, and adapt to Mars' harsh conditions, aiming to transform the barren landscape into a thriving ecosystem.
contributions: Inventory System — Allows players to pick up, store and use items.
Gardening System — Enables players to plant seeds into pots and grow vegetables.
Energy Power System — Manages resource required for gardening tasks.
Water Power System — Manages resource required for gardening tasks.
Time, Day, and Night Cycles — Creates a dynamic day system to simulate time passing.
UI System — Provides intuitive navigation for players.
Setting System — Allows players to adjust game settings.
Movement Mechanic — Includes walking and interacting within the environment.
Shop System — Allows players to buy and sell items.
Cooking System — Allows player to Cooking any foods.
Dialog System — Provides story and information to players.
Quest System — Provides objectives and rewards for players.
Tutorial System — Guides players through the game's mechanics.

title: Kadet Soewoko VR
summary: A VR experience introducing the story of national hero Kadet Soewoko, built for a research collaboration with the Lamongan government and tourism department.
overview: Kadet Soewoko VR is a virtual reality game created as part of a lecturer's research project in collaboration with the Lamongan government and the tourism department. This project aims to introduce the story of Kadet Soewoko, a national hero, through an interactive and immersive VR experience. Players can explore historical events and learn about his heroic deeds.

Kadet Soewoko was a young air force cadet who courageously defended Indonesia during the early days of its independence. Despite limited resources and training, he played a vital role in defending the nation's sovereignty, showing unwavering dedication and bravery. His actions inspire future generations to value patriotism and resilience.
contributions: Interact Raycast System — Enables players to point their gaze or controller at objects and interact, such as reading information or triggering events related to Kadet Soewoko's story.
Pick-Up Mechanic — Allows players to grab and move objects in the game, such as documents or artifacts that provide context about Kadet Soewoko's heroism.
Movement System — Designed to let players explore the environment smoothly and comfortably in VR, including teleportation and smooth locomotion options.
contributionIntro: I contributed as a programmer responsible for implementing the interact raycast system, pick-up mechanics, and player movement system. These mechanics enable players to interact with objects, navigate the environment smoothly, and fully immerse themselves in the historical narrative.

title: Finding Fungus: The Magical Mushroom
summary: A 3D adventure RPG for Android that teaches players about edible, poisonous and rare mushrooms — built by a team of five over four months.
overview: Finding Fungus is a 3D Adventure RPG game created as a project in the GameTech study program. Developed by a team of five over four months in the second semester, this Android game introduces players to various types of mushrooms, including edible, poisonous, and rare species, along with their habitats and Latin names.

The story follows Alice, the main character, on a quest to rescue her kidnapped grandmother from a witch. Players must gather special stones to fulfill the witch's demands, but they face monsters along the journey to obtain these stones.
contributions: Item Pickup Mechanic — Allows players to collect mushrooms in the game world.
Inventory System — Stores collected mushrooms for easy access.
Shop System — Enables players to trade inventory items for items in the shop.
Crafting System — Allows players to combine items to create new ones.
Quest System — Guides players to complete tasks and progress through the game.
UI Navigation System — Provides intuitive menu navigation for the game interface.
Minimap — Guides players through the game world and tracks their location.
Movement & Combat Mechanics — Includes character movement, attack combos, spinning attacks, and a basket-throwing feature.
Dialogue System — Provides story progression and character interactions.
Cutscene System — Plays animated sequences to advance the story.
Encyclopedia System — Provides information on mushrooms, including their Latin names and habitats.
AI Enemy Behavior — Controls enemy movement and attack patterns.

title: YUFO: New Planet
summary: An arcade shooter made in 2.5 days at the PENS Internal GameJam: pilot a UFO and destroy cities to collect resources.
overview: Yufo is a Shooter game created during PENS' Internal GameJam, hosted by GADAS in collaboration with GameTech PENS. This 2.5-day event followed an Arcade theme, with a story of aliens attacking planets to seek new resources. Players gain points by destroying cities and buildings.
Players take on the role of aliens piloting a UFO, tasked with destroying cities and buildings to accumulate points by clearing obstacles in the search for planetary resources.
contributions: Flying Mechanic — Allows the UFO to move up and down with helicopter-like controls.
Shooting Mechanic — Enables the UFO to fire missiles at targets.
Health System — Assigns health values to buildings.
Damage System — Reduces building health upon missile impact using Unity Tags.
Score System — Tracks and displays points for each building destroyed.
contributionIntro: As a programmer, I collaborated with other team programmers, focusing on key mechanics and visual elements. I explored lockable physics in Unity for buildings and UFOs and learned about customizable Bloom effects in Unity's Material & Tag Inspector, which I applied to bullets. The main challenge was inserting materials into Unity manually, a task I tackled with the assistance of the Game Artist. I implemented mechanics such as a Flying system for UFO movement resembling helicopter controls, a Shooting Mechanic to fire missiles, a Health System for buildings, and a Damage System to apply damage using Unity Tags. I also developed a Score system to track destroyed buildings.

title: Project White
summary: My first 2D game — a casual narrative game about a terminally ill character whose final activities shape the ending.
overview: Project White is my first 2D game, created during the Game Design Connect 3.0 event organized by Gameloft Indonesia. This event allowed programmers and game designers to collaborate on a predetermined theme. We developed a Windows-based casual game with 2D visuals, centered around a terminally ill main character awaiting their final moments. Players can perform various activities, each of which influences the game’s ending.

The story revolves around a main character who is ill and near the end of their life. The character can choose to perform various activities or do nothing, with each choice affecting the game’s ending.
contributions: Watering Mechanic — Enables players to water plants, with animated visuals of water splashing from a teapot for enhanced interaction.
Rubbing Mechanic — Involves rubbing a piece of paper to reveal a hidden image of a flower, adding an engaging, interactive element.
contributionIntro: As the programmer, I was responsible for implementing the mechanics of each minigame requested by the game designer. Initially, I faced challenges due to limited experience with 2D game development, so I collaborated with team members to address potential issues. After gaining a foundational understanding of 2D concepts, I developed all the minigame mechanics.

title: MEMEMORY
summary: A 3D first-person adventure made for an ITB game jam on the theme "MEME": collect memory pieces to restore the Mixsuwe shop.
overview: MEMEMORY is a 3D Adventure FPP game developed for a GameJam hosted by ITB, with participants from various backgrounds. Working in a team with my friends, we created the game for Windows, following the theme of "MEME."

The world in MEMEMORY is taken over by four Mixsuwe mascots, threatening to turn everything into a Mixsuwe shop once the time runs out. Players must collect memory pieces and place them in the Mixsuwe shop to restore it to normal, making the mascots disappear and winning the game.
contributions: Movement Mechanic — Controls player movement and camera rotation in the game.
Interaction System — Allows players to pick up items and interact with the environment.
Detection System — Tracks Mixsuwe shop with mini map and memory progres item.
Memory Placement Mechanic — Enables players to place memory pieces in the Mixsuwe shop to make Mixsuwe shop back to normal.
contributionIntro: As a programmer, I developed the main game mechanics and created an item pickup system prototype. Although I had experience with similar mechanics, integrating items with the UI presented challenges. Through experimentation, I implemented a Movement mechanic for player controls, an Interaction system for picking up items, and a Detection System to manage the UI Memory configuration, allowing players to track whether a memory has been used to transform the Mixsuwe shop back to its original form.

title: SPACE-301
summary: A 3D jet shooter made in seven days for GameJamPlus — destroy endless waves of meteors and enemy planes.
overview: SPACE-301 is a 3D jet plane shooter game developed during the 7-day GameJamPlus event open to all Indonesian citizens. The game features a casual theme where players control a jet to destroy endless waves of meteors and enemy planes while avoiding incoming obstacles. A scoreboard tracks player progress and skills.
contributions: Jet Movement and Control — Provides smooth, responsive movement for the jet, allowing the player to navigate and dodge obstacles effectively.
Meteor Destruction and Particle Effects — Destroys meteors on impact and releases particles sized to match the meteors for a satisfying visual effect.
Meteor Spawning System — Randomly generates meteors of various sizes and rotations to create diverse and unpredictable challenges.
Enemy Plane Spawning and Missile Attack — Spawns enemy planes in unique patterns, each capable of firing missiles at the player's jet to increase difficulty.
UI Navigation — Includes start screen, main menu, loading screen, name entry, and scoreboard to guide players through the game interface.
contributionIntro: As the programmer, I implemented various gameplay mechanics specified by the game design. I learned how to customize particle effects in Unity, ensuring that particles matched the size of larger meteors through various adjustments. I was also responsible for programming the jet movement mechanics, rotation for targeting meteors, and different spawn patterns for meteors and enemy planes. Additionally, I created UI elements such as start screens, loading, main menu, name entry, and scoreboard.

title: Lontong Balap
summary: A split-screen multiplayer racing game with a jungle theme, made in two and a half days.
overview: Lontong Balap is a 3D multiplayer racing game developed in two and a half days during the 11th Internal GameJam. Designed for split-screen play, it follows a Jungle theme, with two players racing on obstacle-filled tracks.
contributions: Driving Mechanics — Core racing controls for player movement.
Split-Screen Camera System — Dual camera views for each player, displaying a third-person perspective.
Obstacle Placement — Track obstacles designed to increase the game’s challenge.
UI Navigation System — Includes loading screens, main menu, and map selection options.
contributionIntro: As the programmer, I focused on creating driving mechanics, implementing split-screen cameras, and setting up track obstacles. I also developed UI navigation elements, including loading screens, a main menu, map selection, and a win/loss system to display race outcomes.

title: SESAT: Tersesat Ohhh Tersesat
summary: A first-person horror shooter made in seven days for the BINUS GameJam: escape a maze haunted by ghosts.
overview: SESAT is a game I made right after being accepted at PENS, working with new team members for the first time. Developed for the 7-day BINUS GameJam, it features a Horror & FPS theme with 3D visuals on Windows.
The player is trapped in an almost inescapable maze, haunted by ghosts lurking around every corner, which must be killed using weapons.
contributions: Pickup Item Mechanic — Allows players to collect items tagged as interactable.
Shooting Mechanic — Allows players to use weapons to attack ghosts.
Movement Mechanism — Character movement mechanics that include basic and advanced movements.
Ghost AI System — Ghosts can chase and attack the player based on proximity.
Damage and Blood System — Applies damage to ghosts and displays UI death for the player.
contributionIntro: As the programmer, this was my first experience creating a First Person game. I learned about FPS mechanics in Unity using the Raycast System through YouTube tutorials. My main challenge was implementing interactions in the game, where I tagged interactable items. I created mechanics like Pickup Item, allowing players to collect tagged items, as well as movement, shooting, and an AI system for ghosts to chase and attack the player. I also developed a Damage and Blood system to deal damage to the ghosts.

title: Pentol Golf
summary: A 3D arcade golf game with levels and obstacles, made in 2.5 days on the theme "Pentol & AirFryer".
overview: Pentol Golf is a 3D Arcade game I created during the Internal GameJam event in the Game Technology program, with a development time limit of 2.5 days. Working in a randomly assigned team, we created a golf-style game with levels and various obstacles, based on the theme “Pentol & AirFryer.”
contributions: Hitting Mechanic — Allows players to hit the golf ball in the desired direction.
Level Terrain — Designed and implemented terrain for levels 1, 2, and 3.
Line Trace System — Determines the direction of the ball before hitting.
contributionIntro: As the programmer, I developed core mechanics and experimented with assets provided by the Game Artist. I learned about Trace line, Physics, and Collision in Unity. Despite time constraints and evolving mechanics from Game Design, I successfully implemented the Hitting mechanic to control the golf ball’s direction. Additionally, I developed Terrain for levels 1, 2, and 3, the Line Trace system to set ball direction, and a UI System for game navigation, including Loading and Main Menu.

title: Gerilya: Dominate Nusantara
summary: A two-player strategy board game, inspired by Monopoly, where colonizers and indigenous people compete for Indonesia's provinces.
overview: This board game, inspired by Monopoly, is set on a map of Indonesia divided into provinces. Played by two players who take turns, each player represents one of two factions: the colonizers or the indigenous people, competing to gain control over regions across the country.

In a struggle for dominance over the Indonesian archipelago, two factions face off—the colonizers, aiming to expand their rule, and the indigenous people, determined to defend their homeland. Players strategically capture provinces, rally support, and build influence, striving to shape the fate of Indonesia.
contributions: Trailer Animation — I animated the Gerilya trailer in Unity, highlighting money, cards, and the territorial struggle.
contributionIntro: As the Game Designer, I was responsible for developing game mechanics, balancing the board elements, and creating strategic objectives for both factions to enhance replayability and immersion. Additionally, as an Animator, I crafted the trailer video in Unity, utilizing Unity Animation to bring the game’s conflict and visuals to life, effectively capturing the tension and excitement of the gameplay.
